grammarNotes.title: On TV, in the paper: in + dative
grammarNotes.body:
Where English says *on TV* or *on the radio*, German says **in**, followed by the dative you know from Unit 12: *in dem* shortens to **im**.

Three words look alike, so keep them apart:

- **fernsehen** = to watch TV (a separable verb: *Ich sehe fern.*)
- **der Fernseher** = the TV set, the machine
- **das Fernsehen** = television as a medium: **im Fernsehen** = on TV

**die Nachrichten** (the news) is plural in German, so the verb is plural too: *Die Nachrichten **kommen** um acht Uhr.* With *kommen*, German says what's *on*: **Was kommt heute im Fernsehen?** = What's on TV today?

*Radio hören* needs no article: *Ich höre Radio.*
table: Ich höre die Nachrichten im Radio.
Ich sehe ein Video im Internet.
Ich habe es in der Zeitung gelesen.

grammarNotes.title: wissen: to know
grammarNotes.body:
**wissen** means to know a fact. It's irregular in the singular: the vowel changes to **ei**, and like the modal verbs, **ich** and **er / sie / es** look the same and have no ending. The plural is regular.

- **Ich weiß nicht.** = I don't know.
- **Das weiß ich nicht.** = I don't know that.

To know a person or a place, German uses a different verb, which comes later.

Two short answers with **glauben**:

- **Ich glaube schon.** = I think so.
- **Ich glaube nicht.** = I don't think so.

Here *schon* doesn't mean *already*: it just makes the answer a yes.

grammarNotes.title: dass: that, with the verb at the end
grammarNotes.body:
**dass** (that) joins two sentences, usually after a verb of thinking or saying: *glauben, denken, wissen, sagen, hoffen*.

Just like **weil**, dass sends the verb to the **very end** of its part of the sentence. A **comma** always comes before *dass*.

- *Er ist krank.* → *Ich glaube, dass er krank **ist**.*

Separable verbs join back into one word at the end: *Der Film fängt um acht an.* → *Ich glaube, dass der Film um acht Uhr **anfängt**.*

To say you *don't* think so, put **nicht** after *glaube*, like English *I don't think*: *Ich glaube **nicht**, dass er kommt.*

In speech you'll also hear *dass* left out, like English *I think he's ill*. Then the second part keeps its normal order: *Ich glaube, er **ist** krank.*

**dass** and **das** sound exactly the same. *dass* with double s joins sentences; *das* means *the* or *that one*.

grammarNotes.title: konnte, musste, wollte, sollte
grammarNotes.body:
Remember **war** and **hatte**? The modal verbs have short past forms too, and Germans use them instead of the Perfekt. This past form is called the **Präteritum**.

- The **umlaut disappears**: *können → konnte, müssen → musste*.
- The endings are exactly like **hatte**: *ich* and *er / sie / es* look the same and have no extra ending.
- The other verb still waits at the end: *Ich **musste** gestern lange **arbeiten**.*

**möchten** has no past of its own: use **wollte**. *Ich möchte ins Kino gehen* → *Gestern **wollte** ich ins Kino gehen.*

You'll also hear *du solltest* meaning *you should* as advice. Same form, but for now learn it as the past.

grammarNotes.title: dass with two verbs
grammarNotes.body:
When the sentence has two verbs (a modal verb, or the Perfekt), the infinitive or participle goes near the end as usual, and the **conjugated verb goes after it, right at the end**. This works the same after *weil*.

- *Er kann kommen.* → *Ich hoffe, dass er kommen **kann**.*
- *Er hat angerufen.* → *Sie sagt, dass er gestern angerufen **hat**.*
- *Ich musste arbeiten.* → *…, weil ich arbeiten **musste**.*

A whole story about yesterday can mix all of this: *Gestern **konnte** ich nicht kommen, weil ich arbeiten **musste**.*

exercises.title: Zeitung, Radio, Fernseher
exercises.body:
Welcome to A2! This unit is about the media.

- **die Zeitung** = the newspaper
- **das Radio** = the radio
- **der Fernseher** = the TV set

You know **fernsehen** (to watch TV) and **lesen, hören, sehen** from Unit 9. *der Fernseher* is the machine itself.

**Radio hören** needs no article: *Ich höre Radio.*

examples.translation: The TV is new.

examples.translation: In the evening I watch TV.

exercises.title: die Nachrichten: the news
exercises.body:
**die Nachrichten** = the news. It's the plural of *die Nachricht* (message) from Unit 14: the news is lots of messages!

In English *news* is singular, but in German it's **plural**, so the verb is plural too: *Die Nachrichten **kommen** um acht Uhr.* With *kommen*, German says what's *on*.

- **die Sendung** = the programme, the show (on TV or radio)
- **interessant** = interesting. Stress at the end: *in-te-re-SANT*.

exercises.title: im Fernsehen: on TV
exercises.body:
Where English says *on TV* or *on the radio*, German says **in**, with the dative from Unit 12:

- **im Fernsehen** = on TV (*das Fernsehen* is television itself, not the TV set)
- **im Radio** = on the radio
- **in der Zeitung** = in the newspaper

A question you'll use a lot: **Was kommt heute im Fernsehen?** = What's on TV today?

exercises.title: Internet, Computer, App, Video
exercises.body:
Lots of media words come from English. Only the sound is German:

- **das Internet** = the internet. **im Internet** = on the internet (in + dem again).
- **der Computer** = the computer: *kom-PYOO-ter*
- **die App** = the app: it rhymes with *step*
- **das Video** = the video: *VEE-day-oh*
- **online** = online, just like English

exercises.body:
- **die Serie** = the series, on TV or online. Plural: *die Serien*.
- **gerade** = at the moment, right now. It goes after the verb.

To ask a friend what they're watching: **Welche Serie siehst du gerade?** Remember *sehen → du siehst, er sieht*, and *welche* for a *die* word.

exercises.title: glauben, denken, sagen, hoffen
exercises.body:
Four verbs for opinions and news. They're all regular: *ich glaube, du glaubst, er glaubt*.

- **glauben** = to believe, to think
- **denken** = to think
- **sagen** = to say, to tell
- **hoffen** = to hope

*glauben* and *denken* both work for *I think*. *Ich glaube* is a little less sure.

exercises.title: Ich glaube schon. Ich glaube nicht.
exercises.body:
Two short answers for when you're not 100% sure:

- **Ich glaube schon.** = I think so.
- **Ich glaube nicht.** = I don't think so.

Here *schon* doesn't mean *already*: it just turns the answer into a yes. You'll also hear **Ich denke schon.**

exercises.title: dass: that
exercises.body:
To say *what* you think, know, say or hope, join two sentences with **dass** (that).

Just like **weil**, *dass* sends the verb to the **very end**. A **comma** always comes before *dass*:

- *Er ist krank.* → *Ich glaube, dass er krank **ist**.*
- *Die Sendung kommt um acht.* → *Ich weiß, dass die Sendung um acht Uhr **kommt**.*

In speech, people sometimes leave out *dass*. Then the verb stays second, as in a normal sentence: *Ich glaube, er **ist** krank.* Both are right.

*dass* sounds exactly like *das*: a short *a*.

exercises.title: wichtig, and separable verbs after dass
exercises.body:
**wichtig** = important.

Separable verbs like *anfangen* and *anrufen* split up in a normal sentence. After *dass*, the verb is at the end, so the two parts **join back into one word**:

- *Der Film fängt um acht Uhr an.* → *Ich glaube, dass der Film um acht Uhr **anfängt**.*
- *Sie ruft heute an.* → *Ich hoffe, dass sie heute **anruft**.*

lessons.title: I couldn't come: konnte and musste

exercises.title: konnte: could
exercises.body:
Remember **war** and **hatte** from Unit 14? The modal verbs have short past forms too, and Germans use them instead of the Perfekt.

**können → konnte** = could, was able to. The **umlaut disappears**!

The endings are exactly like *hatte*:

- ich **konnte**
- du **konntest**
- er / sie / es **konnte**
- wir **konnten**, ihr **konntet**, sie / Sie **konnten**

The other verb still waits at the end: *Ich **konnte** gestern nicht **kommen**.*

accepted: konnte
exercises.translation: I couldn't come yesterday.

exercises.title: musste, wollte, sollte
exercises.body:
The other modal verbs work the same way:

- **müssen → musste** = had to (no umlaut here either)
- **wollen → wollte** = wanted to
- **sollen → sollte** = was supposed to

**möchten** has no past of its own, so use **wollte**: *Ich möchte ins Kino gehen* → *Gestern **wollte** ich ins Kino gehen.*

exercises.title: Telling a story about yesterday
exercises.body:
When you talk about the past, use:

- the **Perfekt** for most verbs: *Ich habe ferngesehen.*
- **war** and **hatte** for *sein* and *haben*
- **konnte, musste, wollte, sollte** for the modal verbs

After **weil**, the modal verb goes right to the end, after the other verb: *…, weil ich arbeiten **musste**.*

After **dass**, the same thing happens as after *weil*. With a modal verb or the Perfekt, the infinitive or participle comes first, and the **conjugated verb goes right at the end**:

- *Er kann kommen.* → *Ich hoffe, dass er kommen **kann**.*
- *Er hat angerufen.* → *Sie sagt, dass er gestern angerufen **hat**.*
- *Sie ist nach Hause gegangen.* → *Ich glaube, dass sie nach Hause gegangen **ist**.*

examples.text: Oh nein! Ich wollte am Samstag ins Kino gehen.
examples.translation: Jonas: Oh no! I wanted to go to the cinema on Saturday.

examples.text: Dann nimm das Fahrrad oder den Bus!
examples.translation: Mia: Then take your bike or the bus!

examples.text: Gute Idee! Und was machst du heute Abend?
examples.translation: Jonas: Good idea! And what are you doing this evening?

examples.text: Ich bleibe zu Hause und sehe meine Serie.
examples.translation: Mia: I'm staying at home and watching my series.

examples.text: Welche Serie siehst du gerade?
examples.translation: Jonas: Which series are you watching at the moment?

examples.text: Eine Serie aus Deutschland. Sie ist sehr spannend! Gestern habe ich drei Folgen gesehen.
examples.translation: Mia: A series from Germany. It's really exciting! Yesterday I watched three episodes.

examples.text: Drei Folgen? Und heute musstest du um sechs Uhr aufstehen!
examples.translation: Jonas: Three episodes? And today you had to get up at six!

examples.text: Ich weiß! Ich bin sehr müde. Aber die Serie ist so spannend!
examples.translation: Mia: I know! I'm very tired. But the series is so exciting!

examples.text: Ich wollte die Serie auch sehen, aber ich hatte keine Zeit.
examples.translation: Jonas: I wanted to watch the series too, but I didn't have time.

examples.text: Du musst die Serie sehen! Ich weiß, dass du gern Serien siehst.
examples.translation: Mia: You have to watch the series! I know that you like watching series.

examples.text: Okay! Ich hoffe, dass ich am Wochenende Zeit habe. Dann sehe ich die Serie online.
examples.translation: Jonas: Okay! I hope that I have time at the weekend. Then I'll watch the series online.

exercises.instruction: From the conversation: why didn't Jonas see the news?
